title: The Rug Gives Way
description: The floor looks solid. It is not. Your foot comes down on the moth-eaten runner and the boards beneath flex sharply — a hollow sound, a crack, and then the whole section tilts. The gap beneath is black and deeper than it should be. You have perhaps a second.

choices.label: Throw your weight back immediately
choices.description: Drop your momentum and lunge backward before the boards give entirely.

success.narrative: You land hard on solid floor, breath knocked out, but safe.

failure.narrative: Your heel catches the edge and you go down, one leg plunging into the gap before you drag yourself clear.

choices.label: Leap forward across the gap
choices.description: Push off the failing boards and clear the rotten section entirely.

success.narrative: You clear it cleanly, landing in a crouch on solid stone beyond the runner. You mentally clap at your own athleticism.

failure.narrative: You do not get enough distance. The far edge crumbles and you drop, catching a beam with both arms before the dark takes you.

choices.label: Drop flat and distribute your weight
choices.description: Go to the floor immediately, spreading yourself across the failing section.

success.narrative: The boards hold under your spread weight. You crawl to solid ground, slow and deliberate.

failure.narrative: The instinct to scramble overrides the plan. One board cracks under a knee and the splinters open your leg.

visual.alt_text: A grand entry hall floor, an old rug peeling back at a splintered gap in the boards, darkness visible beneath. The edges of the hole are pale and raw.
